failure_caught: Without the size guard one tailnet client could declare a huge Content-Length and occupy one of the 24 connection slots while the process grows its buffer; accepting Transfer-Encoding: chunked or a folded header reintroduces the framing disagreement with the fronting proxy that lets a second request slip past the login check in authorized(), i.e. request smuggling into the session control API.
criticality_reason: This is the input-hardening boundary in front of an API that can read every terminal and send keystrokes; a framing or memory regression threatens the availability and the access gate of the whole remote surface (src/remote/mod.rs:126-166), not just a display detail.
signal_reason: Three exact rejections sit on real boundaries: MAX_BODY + 1, a chunked request, and a folded header (src/remote/http.rs:322-330); MAX_BODY itself, a body longer than its declared Content-Length, and the error kind are not asserted.
uniqueness_reason: No other test sends oversized, chunked or folded-header requests: tests/remote_web.rs:30-56 only writes well-formed GET/POST requests, so this failure mode has no other evidenced protection.
fidelity_reason: The production read_request is exercised directly, so the guards under test are the shipped ones (src/remote/http.rs:119-200); only the transport is a Cursor instead of a TcpStream.
recommendation_reason: The only protection for the gateway's framing and size guards, which are security-relevant and unreachable from the acceptance harness; it must stay.
